checked_contracts: The MethodAnalysisContext plain-range overload intentionally queries the original registered pointer; GetRawBytesForMethod and GetIsilFromMethod explicitly use the app+analysisAddress overload, so a selected8-byte wrapper is not mistaken for its unboxed analysis body.
Eligibility uses the per-application ConditionalWeakTable state and existing frame-cache lock. It does not change registered pointers, managed identities, selected mappings or alias registration.

CIE descriptions retain the original supported version/encoding parse and a separate exact-zR property. FDE ranges retain size plus Plain=(exact zR and zero FDE augmentation). zPLR, unknown augmentation and nonempty/truncated FDE augmentation do not become plain.

The existing general bounds API still returns a valid zPLR range size and still permits valid nonempty augmentation; only the new plain API uses the extra eligibility flag. Shared positive/negative cache state does not replace or poison the general range result.

Exact lookup retains aligned indexed start, positive aligned length, text-segment/record bounds, exact initial-location agreement, expected0x1B encoding and the next independently indexed function boundary. False plain queries return size0.

New ordinary raw-byte selection requires a real metadata Definition and excludes attribute generators. It maps the exact analysis address, checks raw-size bounds, and GetIsil requires the exact certified RawBytes length before disassembling that body.

The existing CFG matcher is byte-for-byte unchanged. Known metadata/class initializer identities remain distinct. Class acceptance keeps X0 receiver loads, rejects W0 flag/finished clobbers, checks direct interior predecessor uniqueness and cold-helper predecessor identity, proves flag liveness and equivalent joins, and rejects unsupported field-reload shapes.

Accepted class sites still emit an explicit semantic CallVoid(known helper,X0) at the native guard start followed by a jump to the proven join. The class load and scheduled field/arithmetic instructions before that start remain. KFR must separately establish the exact original represented class before emitting RunClassConstructor; unknown class origins do not become no-ops.

Only the separately proven metadata-assurance flag load becomes a constant; intervening approved scheduled instructions remain and flag death is checked. No original game-field initializer/store/reload is generalized into a compiler flag.

The pre-existing sequential ordinary path remains for compatibility. For a newly eligible plain ordinary body its general exact-range query necessarily succeeds under the same NSO24 opt-in, so that path retains a semantic constructor request rather than its legacy no-op fallback.
